howToUse: This is your "Is My Niche Real" Script Bank — a set of word-for-word scripts for the three conversations that will surface in your first week inside the programme before your niche is finalised. Open it the moment doubt, a partner's question, or a networking opportunity arrives, find the right script, and read it aloud or copy it verbatim. You do not need a polished niche to use any of these — that is the point.
promise: Use these scripts to move through the three hardest early conversations without stalling, so that doubt, a spouse's scepticism, or an unexpected "so what do you do?" never becomes a reason to pause. You stay in motion while the niche work gets done inside the programme.
tools:
[
  {
    "name": "The Inner-Doubt Interrupt: What to Say to Yourself",
    "type": "script",
    "instructions": "Read this aloud — or into a voice note to yourself — the moment 'I need to finalise my niche first' surfaces as a reason not to act.",
    "content": "## The Inner-Doubt Interrupt

**When to use it:** The moment you catch yourself thinking any version of *"I'm not ready," "I don't know my niche yet," or "I should figure this out before I commit."**

---

### What the thought is actually doing

The thought feels logical because it sounds responsible. It isn't stopping you because the niche is genuinely unclear — it's stopping you because naming the niche out loud is the moment *reversible* becomes *irreversible*, and every professional instinct you developed in a corporate environment trained you to research before you commit. That instinct served you there. Here it is keeping the notes app closed.

The niche is not the thing you figure out alone first and then bring into the work. The niche is the thing the work produces. Waiting to start until it's done is waiting to start until you've already finished.

---

### Say this to yourself — exactly

> *"I have spent [X] years developing expertise in [FORMER FIELD/ROLE — e.g., regulatory compliance, paediatric occupational therapy, brand strategy]. I am not starting from zero. I am starting from somewhere very specific, and the reason I cannot see the exact offer yet is that I have not yet had the structured process that separates my real expertise from the professional identity I performed at [FORMER COMPANY / IN THAT INDUSTRY]. That process is what I am walking into. My job right now is not to have the answer — it is to show up so the answer can be found."*

---

### The follow-up anchor (write this on a card and keep it visible)

> *"Clarity is not a prerequisite for starting. Clarity is a product of starting."*

---

### If the doubt comes back a second time in the same day

Say this:

> *"The doubt coming back is not evidence that I was wrong to start. It is evidence that I am at the exact point where the work matters. I am going to do one specific thing from the programme right now — not think about the doubt, not research the doubt — one thing. Then I will reassess."*

Then open the programme and do the next step."
  },
  {
    "name": "The Partner / Spouse Script: Answering 'Are You Sure Yet?'",
    "type": "script",
    "instructions": "Use this script — or lift sentences from it verbatim — the next time your partner or spouse asks whether you've figured out your niche, whether this is 'really happening,' or whether you're sure.",
    "content": "## The Partner / Spouse Script

**When to use it:** Any conversation where your partner asks a version of *"So do you know what you're doing yet?" / "Have you decided on your niche?" / "Are you sure this is the right direction?"*

---

### Before you open your mouth: what this conversation is actually about

Your partner is not asking because they doubt you. They are asking because they are watching someone they love make a significant decision and they cannot yet see the shape of it — and uncertainty about the shape reads, to a partner, as uncertainty about the commitment. Your job in this conversation is not to prove the niche is real. Your job is to make the commitment legible, even while the niche is still being built.

---

### Script A — When the question is gentle / curious

*"Are you any closer to knowing what you want to focus on?"*

**Your answer:**

> *"I am — and I want to explain how this actually works, because I spent a long time thinking I needed to figure out the niche before I could do anything, and that's not how it works. What I've signed up for is a structured process that starts with [FORMER PROFESSIONAL ROLE/FIELD — e.g., 'my compliance background,' 'my years in brand strategy,' 'what I was actually doing day-to-day as a project lead'] and systematically identifies which part of that is a real consulting offer — something specific that someone will pay for — versus the background knowledge I was just expected to have. I'm not starting from scratch. I'm starting from twelve years of real work. The programme is what turns that into a clear offer. So 'not having my niche yet' isn't a sign I'm lost — it's literally the starting point the programme is designed for."*

---

### Script B — When the question has an edge / carries concern about money or time

*"I just want to know you're not spending money on something you're not even sure about yet."*

**Your answer:**

> *"I hear you, and I want to give you a real answer rather than a reassuring one. What I'm sure about is this: I have [X years] of professional experience in [FIELD], I left work to raise [our/the] kids and I did that, and I am not willing to go back into a salaried role or do another degree just to re-enter the workforce. This is the most direct path from where I am to earning — and specifically, the programme commits to [state the programme guarantee/outcome window, e.g., 'helping me sign three paying clients within 90 days of launching my offer']. I'm not waiting to be sure about my niche before I start — the programme is what produces that clarity. I am sure about starting. That's the decision I've made."*

---

### Script C — The short version for a repeated conversation

*"We've talked about this — are you any further along?"*

**Your answer:**

> *"Yes. I'm inside the process now. The niche gets built through the work, not before it — and I'm doing the work. What would help me most right now is [ONE SPECIFIC THING — e.g., 'an hour on Tuesday mornings that's mine,' 'knowing you're not going to ask me to justify this every week,' 'being able to talk you through what I'm finding as I go']. Can we agree on that?"*

---

### What not to say

❌ *"I'm almost there"* — sets an expectation you cannot keep  
❌ *"I just need a bit more time to think"* — confirms the thing they're worried about  
❌ *"It's complicated"* — closes the conversation and raises their anxiety  

---

**The goal of this conversation is not to win it. It is to make your commitment visible, your process legible, and your ask specific.**"
  },
  {
    "name": "The Network Conversation Script: 'What Do You Do?' Before You Have a Polished Answer",
    "type": "script",
    "instructions": "Use this when someone in your network asks what you're working on — at a school gate, a dinner, a LinkedIn message, or a former colleague catch-up — and you do not yet have a finished niche to give them.",
    "content": "## The Network Conversation Script

**When to use it:** Any real-world or online moment when someone asks *"So what are you up to these days?" / "Are you working again?" / "What are you doing now that the kids are older?"* — and you don't yet have a polished offer statement.

---

### Why this conversation matters right now (before your niche is done)

The people who will refer or become your first clients are already in your network. They are the former colleagues, the school-gate contacts, the LinkedIn connections who already know the professional you were. The instinct to wait until you have a finished niche before talking to them costs you weeks of warm relationship-warming. You do not need a finished offer to have a good conversation. You need a sentence that is honest, specific, and invites a response.

---

### The Bridge Sentence (your core answer — memorise this structure)

> *"I spent [X years] in [FIELD/ROLE — e.g., financial services, NHS commissioning, in-house legal], stepped back when the kids were young, and I'm now setting up a consulting practice that helps [TYPE OF ORGANISATION OR PERSON] with [BROAD PROBLEM AREA — e.g., 'the compliance challenges that come with rapid team growth,' 'the brand positioning decisions that stall a product launch,' 'the HR processes that break down as a company scales past fifty people']. I'm at the stage of working out exactly where to focus, which is the interesting bit — but [FORMER ROLE/EXPERTISE] is the foundation."*

**Fill in your version now and save it in your phone:**

> *"I spent [\_\_\_ years] in [\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_], stepped back when the kids were young, and I'm now setting up a consulting practice that helps [\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_] with [\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_]. I'm at the stage of working out exactly where to focus — but [\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_] is the foundation."*

---

### What to say when they ask a follow-up

**"Oh interesting — what kind of clients are you looking for?"**

> *"Right now I'm having conversations with people in [FORMER INDUSTRY] — particularly anyone dealing with [BROAD PROBLEM AREA]. I'm not in full launch mode yet, but I'm curious: do you know anyone in that world who's navigating something like that?"*

---

**"Do you have a website / something I can look at?"**

> *"Not yet — I'm being deliberate about building the offer properly before I put anything out publicly. But I'd love to stay in touch. Can I connect with you on LinkedIn / drop you my email? When I'm ready to talk specifics, you'll be one of the first people I reach out to."*

---

**"Couldn't you just go back into [FORMER ROLE] full-time?"**

> *"I could — but I'm choosing not to. I have the expertise, and I want to use it on my terms. Consulting is the model that makes sense for where I am now."* *(Then move on. You don't owe them a longer justification.)*

---

### The LinkedIn version (for a message or comment reply)

> *"Thanks for asking — I'm setting up a consulting practice drawing on my background in [FIELD]. Early days, but I'm working with [BROAD CLIENT TYPE] on [BROAD PROBLEM AREA]. Would love to reconnect properly — are you still in [INDUSTRY/ROLE]?"*

---

### What you are NOT doing in this conversation

❌ Apologising for not having a finished answer  
❌ Saying *"I'm still figuring it out"* as your primary statement (it invites pity, not referrals)  
❌ Listing every possible direction you're considering  
❌ Underselling the expertise with *"I was just a [title]"*

**You are a professional re-entering on your own terms. The sentence above reflects that.**"

  {
    "name": "The Niche-Readiness Check: Is This Doubt or Data?",
    "type": "worksheet",
    "instructions": "Run through this before any session where you're tempted to reopen the niche question from scratch — takes under five minutes and tells you whether you're dealing with genuine new information or the same loop in a new outfit.",
    "content": "## The Niche-Readiness Check

**Use it when:** You're about to delay a programme step because you feel like the niche still isn't clear enough, or you want to check whether a new doubt is actually new.

---

### Step 1 — Name the doubt in one sentence

Write exactly what you're telling yourself right now:

> *"I think I need to wait because _______________________________________________"*

---

### Step 2 — Run it through the four questions

Answer yes or no. No explanation needed yet.

| # | Question | Yes / No |
|---|----------|----------|
| 1 | Is this doubt based on something **new** that happened in the last 48 hours — a conversation, a piece of feedback, a specific piece of information? | |
| 2 | Have I had a version of this exact doubt **before** — same feeling, different words? | |
| 3 | If I wait two more weeks, will I actually have **different information** — or just more time? | |
| 4 | Is the thing I'm about to do **inside the programme** — the next step I'm avoiding — something that would help answer this doubt? | |

---

### Step 3 — Read your result

**If you answered YES to Question 1 and NO to Question 2:**  
This may be genuine new data. Bring it to your next programme call or coaching session. Note it here: *"New information: _______________________"* — then continue with the next programme step anyway.

**If you answered YES to Question 2 and/or NO to Question 3:**  
This is the loop, not new data. The doubt has arrived in a slightly different outfit. Say the Inner-Doubt Interrupt script (Tool 1), then open the programme and do the next step.

**If you answered YES to Question 4:**  
The programme step you're avoiding is the answer to the doubt you're feeling. Do that step first. The doubt will have less room when you come back to it.

---

### Step 4 — The one-line commitment

Write this and date it:

> *"Today is [DATE]. The next thing I am doing inside the programme is [SPECIFIC STEP]. I am doing it before I reopen the niche question."*

---

**What this worksheet is for:** Distinguishing between doubt that carries real information (rare at this stage) and doubt that is a holding pattern in disguise (common, normal, and not a reason to stop). You will feel the loop many times. That is not a sign you are wrong. It is a sign you are at the edge of something real."
  }

nextStep.body: You have the words for the three conversations that will try to stop you before the niche is clear. Now it's time to start building the niche itself. Your first session inside the programme is where the Career Layer Excavation Process begins — starting not with a blank worksheet but with your actual career history, the roles you held, the relationships you navigated, and the expertise that lived underneath the identity your industry built around you. That session is where 'I don't know which idea is real' becomes a specific, nameable offer you can say out loud. Come in with the notes app open — every idea you've written there is material, not noise.
